title: Power Automate
seoTitle: Power Automate Consultant & Workflow Automation | EfiOps
metaDescription: Automate reminders, approvals, alerts and recurring admin with Microsoft Power Automate. Practical workflows scoped around your business process.
h1: Keep work moving. Lose the chasing.
eyebrow: Power Automate · A dependable next step
lead: A quote needs following up. An approval is waiting. A review is due. Turn the steps someone has to remember into workflows with clear rules—and a visible place for exceptions.

sections.heading: Some work only happens because somebody remembers.
paragraphs: A review becomes due. A forecast changes. An approval is waiting. Someone opens a spreadsheet, checks the dates and sends the same message again.
That routine is a good place to look for automation—provided the rules are clear and somebody can see when an exception needs attention.

sections.heading: Useful automation starts with a dependable process.
items: Scheduled reminders. Trigger the next step from dates, status changes or defined business rules.
Approvals and routing. Send requests to the right person and keep the decision attached to the record.
Change alerts. Compare information and notify people when an agreed threshold or condition is met.
Connected admin. Move suitable information between Microsoft tools, databases, forms and supported services.
Existing flow repairs. Investigate failed conditions, missing values, duplicate actions and unreliable runs.

sections.heading: Built for the ordinary day—and the awkward one.
paragraphs: We define the trigger, the records involved, the people responsible and what should happen when information is missing. The workflow is then tested with ordinary cases, date boundaries, repeated runs and exceptions.
You receive a clear explanation of the flow and its dependencies. Any licensing or connector requirements are checked before the implementation is agreed.

faqs.question: Can you fix a flow we already use?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can inspect the intended process, reproduce the issue where access allows and propose a focused repair.

faqs.question: Can reminders be sent to different managers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Routing can follow defined data and rules, with an agreed fallback when the usual recipient is missing.

faqs.question: Can a workflow connect to SQL?
faqs.answer: It can be scoped around supported connections and appropriate permissions. Access, hosting and licensing need to be checked for the particular database.

faqs.question: How do we avoid sending the same notification twice?
faqs.answer: The design should track what has already happened and test repeated runs. The exact method depends on the workflow and its record system.

cta.label: Discuss a workflow
cta.heading: Which repeated task would you like to stop chasing?
cta.text: Describe the trigger, the steps and the tools involved. We can work out whether the process is ready to automate.

primaryIntent: Power Automate consultant; Microsoft workflow automation.
summary: Keep reminders, approvals and recurring admin moving without the repeated checks.

useCases.title: The quote is sent. Then what?
useCases.body: Prepare the next follow-up when no reply arrives, and stop the reminder when the conversation moves forward.

useCases.title: The review date shouldn’t be a surprise.
useCases.body: Route due reviews to the right manager, with a clear fallback when a recipient or date is missing.

useCases.title: Tell me when the plan changes.
useCases.body: Compare new forecasts with the agreed baseline and flag the changes that actually need attention.

journey.heading: From a sent quote to a follow-up that knows when to stop.
journey.example: A service business wants every quote to have a clear next step.
journey.question: Who follows up, and when?
scope: Prepare follow-up after two working days
Stop the reminder when a reply arrives
journey.boundary: Automatic pricing and a full customer portal are outside this first workflow.

stages.label: Understand
stages.title: Follow one enquiry through the business.
stages.body: We trace how an enquiry is captured, where the quote is recorded and who owns the conversation. The important gaps are often between tools, where someone has to copy details or remember a reminder.
stages.output: A process map, system inventory and named task owners.

stages.label: Agree
stages.title: Define the rule—and the stopping rule.
stages.body: The first scope prepares a follow-up after two working days without a reply. We agree review and approval steps, account access and service costs. A customer reply must change the scheduled next action.
stages.output: An agreed trigger, approval rule and exception path.

stages.label: Build
stages.title: Connect the steps and review the record.
stages.body: The team sees the enquiry, quote status, owner and next action together. We review the message and the condition that prepares it before enabling any agreed sending behaviour.
stages.output: A reviewable workflow with visible status and ownership.

stages.label: Test
stages.title: Try the cases that change the next step.
stages.body: We check waiting quotes, received replies, missing email addresses and repeat triggers. A run history should explain what happened and leave failed or held work with someone who can resolve it.
stages.output: Checks for normal runs, duplicates and held tasks.

stages.label: Hand over
stages.title: Make the workflow understandable to its owner.
stages.body: The handover explains the triggers, connections and review queue. We identify who maintains account permissions, monitors failed runs and approves any future rule changes.
stages.output: A run guide, connection inventory and monitoring responsibilities.

tests.label: No reply
tests.reason: The owner reviews the message before sending.

tests.label: Reply arrives
tests.reason: Keep the conversation with its owner.

tests.label: Email missing
tests.reason: Do not attempt to send; show the missing field to the owner.

handover.title: Workflow rules
handover.body: Triggers, delays, stopping conditions and approval steps.

handover.title: Connections & ownership
handover.body: Accounts, permissions, third-party costs and the person responsible for failed runs.

handover.title: Exception guide
handover.body: How to review held records, correct a missing field and retry without duplication.
